Repair User Guide — Factory

Type 2: Not Under Warranty (Without Serial No.) — Tested OK

Source: Odoo Tour Recorder export — Tour/1B. Repair User Guide - Factory [ Not Under Warranty (Without Serial No ) - Tested Ok ].json

Scenario: The product's warranty period has expired and it has no serial number. The technician tests the item and it is OK, so it is returned to the customer without a quotation or payment.
Every screenshot below is a real capture from a single, clean, fully-passing automated run — taken before each step's action, with the element to use framed in red.

1. Overview

This manual explains how to register and complete a factory repair for an out-of-warranty product with no serial number when the technician finds the item Tested OK — nothing needs repairing. The process runs from the Helpdesk ticket at the receiving branch, through the factory, and ends when the item is dispatched back to the customer.

Ticket stages covered

New Sent to Factory Received at Factory Repair Completed Sent to Sales Centre Received at Sales Centre Handed Over to Customer

Before you start

  • You have access to the Helpdesk, Field Service and Inventory apps.
  • The active company (top bar) is Jinasena Agricultural Machinery (Pvt) Ltd.
  • The customer and product already exist in Odoo (Contacts and Product Master).
  • The item has been physically brought to the branch by the customer.

Section A — Create the Repair Ticket (Steps 1–11)

1 Open the HelpDesk app
NavigationOdoo Home → Apps
ActionClick the Helpdesk app icon on the home screen.
DescriptionOpens the Helpdesk Overview dashboard, showing every support team you have access to.
Odoo Apps home screen — Helpdesk app icon
2 Open the repair tickets
NavigationHelpdesk → Overview → Customer Care - Repair
ActionOn the Customer Care - Repair team card, click Tickets.
DescriptionOpens the list of repair tickets already created for the team.
Helpdesk Overview — Tickets button on the Customer Care - Repair team card
3 Create a new ticket
NavigationHelpdesk → Customer Care - Repair (Tickets)
ActionClick New at the top-left of the ticket list.
DescriptionOpens a blank Helpdesk ticket form for the repair item received from the customer.
All Tickets list — New button
4 Assign the ticket to yourself
NavigationNew ticket form
ActionClick Assign to Me in the status bar.
DescriptionSaves the ticket for the first time and assigns it to the current user. This also generates the ticket's sequence-based name (e.g. REPAIR/2026/01601) — the ticket has no user-editable title.
Blank new ticket form — Assign to Me button
5 Set the repair Type
NavigationTicket form → Type field
ActionClick the Type field and select Repair - Not Under Warranty (Without Serial No.).
DescriptionClassifies items whose warranty has expired and that have no serial number. The field is a many2one autocomplete listing the repair types configured in Studio.
Ticket form — Type field
6 Set the Return Receipt Location
NavigationTicket form → Return Receipt Location field
ActionClick Return Receipt Location and select the branch receiving the item (e.g. BR-AM/Stock, Jinasena Ampara Branch).
DescriptionThe location where the repaired item will be received back for the customer.
Ticket form — Return Receipt Location field
7 Select the Repair Reason
NavigationTicket form → Repair Reason field
ActionClick Repair Reason and select the reported fault (e.g. Difficult to start the engine).
DescriptionChoose the common error that best matches the customer's complaint. This is a many2many tags field; at least one reason is required before the item can be returned.
Ticket form — Repair Reason field
8 Select the Job Location
NavigationTicket form → Job Location field
ActionIn Job Location, select Factory Repair.
DescriptionDefines where the repair is performed. Factory Repair routes the item through Send to Factory / Received at Factory.
Ticket form — Job Location field
9 Select the Customer
NavigationTicket form → Customer field
ActionClick Customer and select KURUNEGALA CASH CUSTOMER.
DescriptionEmail and Phone are filled automatically from the customer record.
Ticket form — Customer field
10 Select the Product
NavigationTicket form → Product field
ActionClick Product and select [JMC6] Multi Chopper 6Hp (Tractor Type).
DescriptionThe repair item from the Product Master. Once Customer, Product and Repair Reason are set, the Create Serial No button appears.
Ticket form — Product field
11 Create a temporary serial number
NavigationTicket form → status bar
ActionClick Create Serial No.
DescriptionThis repair type has no manufacturer serial number, so the system generates a temporary one (equal to the ticket number). Save the ticket first if it has pending changes.
Ticket form — Create Serial No button

QA notes
  • Steps 1-18 are identical to the "Full Flow" (1A) guide; only the task-completion and return legs (steps 19-26) differ: Tested OK replaces diagnosis / image / parts / quotation / deposit / delivery chain / balance payment.
  • The Return button (fix_repair_action_direct_return) raises "You may only return Done pickings" server-side but still creates the Returned Picking first. The automated run calls it, swallows the error, then validates the resulting picking via /web/dataset/call_kw (the picking's Validate button is hidden/unreliable under the Studio views).
  • The Returned Picking opens as a full page here (not a dialog), so the tour step "Close" after the first Validate has no separate screen; the dispatch Validate/Close at the end do use a dialog.
  • Send to Sales Centre and Dispatch become visible only after a full page reload once the previous action completes (computed task_done / stage state). A hash-only navigation does not refresh the record, so the automated flow uses page.reload() in a polling loop.
  • The tour records Tested OK by button[name="2316"] (an action id that differs per database); the automated flow matches it by its label instead. Mark as done / Validate use data-hotkey="v" in the tour; the flow matches by label.
  • Repair Reason is selected before Customer/Product (tour order); Customer and Product each trigger an onchange re-render, so the flow waits about 1 second after each commit.
  • Each screenshot is captured immediately before the step's action with the target element framed in red (a temporary CSS outline applied to the live element only for the capture). Screenshots come from one clean, fully-passing automated run against the staging instance.
  • The "Add Data" toast notifications on the Tested OK screenshot (diagnosis/image not set) are expected for this shortcut path; they do not block the flow.
  • The staging database is a temporary Odoo.sh environment, automatically deleted on 12 October 2026; regenerate the screenshots on the production instance if needed.
